action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The model's long-run posture is still to grow acquisition, but this is a week to apply it carefully rather than push. A Rally watch drop window is open, Bitcoin is down about 12% in a month and now sits just under its 200-day average, and the mood is in extreme fear. Keep acquisition running at a steady pace with trust and education angles, hold trader-focused promotions and keep a reserve; speed up only if price wins back $73,058 and, for a bigger push, $80,625.

reasons: The 200-day average ($73,058) is still rising, about 5% over 90 days.
Up about 13% over 90 days; about 94% of those days closed above the long-term average.
But BTC ($71,514) is now about 2% under that average and down about 12% in 30 days.
Fear & Greed at 20 (extreme fear); 23 days under the 50-day average ($80,625).
watch: Bitcoin has slipped about 2% under its 200-day average, the line holding up the long-run uptrend, while a Rally watch drop window is open and many people are still betting on a rise with borrowed money. A close back above $73,058 would ease the pressure, while a close below $69,500 would turn the week clearly down and put $68,108 (the 200-week average) in view.
analysis: Bottom line: the long-run picture still leans up, but the coming week looks soft and Bitcoin has just slipped under the line that matters most. At about $71,514 it has closed under its 50-day average for 23 days, sits about 11% below it and about 15% below its 30-day high, and Fear & Greed reads 20 (extreme fear); PANews reported the fall below $72,000 on the day Nvidia's CEO stepped down and US tech stocks dropped. A normal week swings about $4,069, so a close above $73,058 (the 200-day average) would ease the pressure, a close below $69,500 (bottom of a typical week's swing) would turn the week clearly down, and in between it stays choppy. Calm, safety-first messaging fits this week better than promotions.

The next month is mixed. The 90-day numbers still point up, with price about 13% higher and about 94% of those days closing above the long-term average, but the last 30 days are down about 12%, and a lot of people are still betting on a rise with borrowed money, which can make dips sharper. Price must win back $80,625 (the 50-day average) for the month to firm up, and only above $86,603 (the 90-day high) is there real room to climb; while it stays under that average, hold bigger campaign pushes until after the 8 December Fed meeting.

The 3-6 month picture still leans up at a moderate strength, because the 200-day average itself is still rising (about 5% over 90 days), but price is now about 2% under it. For the recovery to stay intact, Bitcoin needs to close back above $73,058 (the 200-day average); if it keeps sliding, $68,108 (the 200-week average) is the next floor, and $124,753 (the all-time high) stays the far marker. A run of closes below the 200-day average would weaken this picture and be the moment to shift budget toward keeping existing users.
